definition: Streams cut, in this order, at: each species' highest observation on each stream line (observation_breaks top_per_species); gradient barriers at the 15, 20, 25 and 30 % classes, kept only where a modelled species' access changes (which the acc token decides); falls; user-definite barriers; user habitat classification end points; crossings. The bundle declares user-definite barriers, their control table and the user habitat classification. Where the cuts fall also moves with the data a build reads, which its log records.

As cut-full-top, but streams are cut at every observation (observation_breaks all) and also at subsurface-flow lines (FWA edge types 1410 and 1425) after user-definite barriers: the cuts bcfishpass makes.

The access rules of link's bcfishpass config: bcfishpass's per-species access gradients and observation lifts (parameters_fresh.csv), its species presence table, and the eight species its rules model (BT, CH, CM, CO, PK, SK, ST, WCT). Spec is a digest of the parsed values (lnk_vocabulary_resolve()).

link's first own access rules (the default config at link 0.69.7). From acc-bcfp: BT lifts on BT and DV records of any date, RB lifts on one RB record, GR, KO and RB are modelled, and link's species presence table (no GR in LARL). Spec is a digest of the parsed values (lnk_vocabulary_resolve()).
Each segment's gradient measured over the segment itself, as fresh computes it on the cut network.
Discharge (mad_m3s) from fwapg's modelled discharge, unfilled.

Discharge (mad_m3s) from wet's fwa_v1_segment_monthly annual pick, with river-polygon main stems (edge 1250) that have none filled from the nearest valued line upstream on the same stream line, else downstream on it, else the largest value on any line upstream (discharge_fill), in the groups whose habitat model reads discharge.

As acc-v1, but fwa_upstream's same-line measure test counts a fish record as upstream of a segment only at least 1 m above the segment's start (include_equivalents false, as bcfishpass reads it), where acc-v1 counted one from 1 m below the start. Its clauses that read watershed codes are unchanged. So the segment starting at a species' highest record on a line no longer reads 2 from that record. Spec is a digest of the parsed values (lnk_vocabulary_resolve()).

As acc-bcfp, but fwa_upstream's same-line measure test counts a fish record as upstream of a segment only at least 1 m above the segment's start, as bcfishpass's own observation walk reads it (FWA_Upstream(..., False, 1)); acc-bcfp counted one from 1 m below the start, so the segment starting at a species' highest record on a line read 2 from that record. Spec is a digest of the parsed values (lnk_vocabulary_resolve()).

As acc-v2, but code 2 counts a fish record of the species in any watershed group upstream of a segment (pipeline: observation_upstream: province), where acc-v2 counted only the segment's own group, so a main stem read as not observed up to its group boundary. Streams are still cut at the group's own records. Spec is a digest of the parsed values and the resolved observation_upstream (lnk_vocabulary_resolve()).

As acc-bcfp-2, but code 2 counts a fish record of the species in any watershed group upstream of a segment wherever a record of the segment's own group, of any species, is also upstream (pipeline: observation_upstream: group_gated, the value when absent): bcfishpass's reading, whose spp CTE reads every group's records and whose INNER JOIN on the same-group ids CTE drops a segment with none. acc-bcfp-2 counted only the segment's own group. Spec is a digest of the parsed values and the resolved observation_upstream (lnk_vocabulary_resolve()).
